label: Chinese takeout
h1: An AI phone host for Chinese takeout
seoTitle: AI phone answering for Chinese takeout | ROAL
description: ROAL is a phone host for Chinese takeout. It answers calls, takes pickup orders from your live menu, and sends clean tickets to the kitchen.
lead: Busy Friday dinner. Wok stations loud. The phone keeps ringing. ROAL answers, takes the order, and sends it to the kitchen screen while your team keeps cooking.
question: How can ROAL handle Chinese takeout phone orders without slowing down the kitchen?
answer: ROAL answers the restaurant’s phone, takes pickup and delivery orders from your live menu, and sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. It can quote ready times, collect names and phone numbers, and handle common menu questions like hours, address, parking, and dish details. It does not take card numbers over the phone.

pains.title: The phone rings when the line is busiest
pains.body: Lunch rush and dinner rush are when callers order most. That is also when the front counter is busy with walk-ins, bags, and pickup names.

pains.title: Orders get noisy and easy to miss
pains.body: Chinese takeout orders often include rice choices, spice levels, extra sauce, and small custom notes. One missed modifier can mean a remake or a callback.

pains.title: People call for simple questions first
pains.body: Callers ask if General Tso’s is ready, whether lunch specials are still on, or if parking is behind the store. Those calls still interrupt the team.

howItHelps.title: Answers in the middle of the rush
howItHelps.body: ROAL can pick up the phone when your staff cannot. It keeps the caller moving instead of sending them to voicemail or a long hold.

howItHelps.title: Takes the whole order clearly
howItHelps.body: It can capture items, sizes, modifiers, and notes. Example: chicken lo mein, no onion, mild sesame chicken, extra wonton soup, and white rice.

howItHelps.title: Sends a clean kitchen ticket
howItHelps.body: The order lands on the kitchen screen with the name, phone number, and ready time. That makes it easier to start the ticket right away.

howItHelps.title: Handles common questions too
howItHelps.body: ROAL can answer hours, address, parking, and menu questions from your live info. If it does not know something, it sends it to you with a summary.

sampleCall.line: Hi. Can I place a pickup order?
Of course. What can I get started for you?

Can I get white rice with the sesame chicken?

sections.h2: What a Chinese takeout phone host should handle
sections.body:
Chinese takeout calls are usually fast and specific. Callers want to order family dinner combos, lunch specials, lo mein, fried rice, dumplings, orange chicken, broccoli chicken, or soups without waiting through a long menu. A good phone host should take the order in plain language, repeat back the details, and quote a ready time the kitchen can use.

ROAL is built for that kind of call. It reads your live menu, so if an item is sold out it will not offer it. It can also answer the easy questions that slow your counter down, like whether you are open for lunch, where to park, or if an item is spicy. If a caller asks about allergy-sensitive food or wants to speak to a manager, it passes that along with a short summary.

sections.h2: A simple setup for a busy shop
sections.body:
Setup is meant to be quick. At [Build a free test host](/try), you can paste your restaurant website, Google Maps link, or just your restaurant name and city. ROAL reads the menu, prices, hours, and address from public pages, and you can also upload a menu file or photos.

Once you like the voice and name, you claim the host and forward your existing number to it. You can forward all calls, or only the ones that are busy or unanswered. That lets you keep your current number while ROAL handles pickup orders during the rush.

sections.h2: Use a worked example before you go live
sections.body:
Say a Friday night brings 12 missed calls while the counter is slammed with pickup bags and steamed rice. With ROAL, those calls can become order tickets instead of voicemail. The kitchen screen shows each ticket as new, preparing, or ready, so the team can work in order.

If a caller asks a question ROAL cannot answer, it goes to your inbox. You answer it once, and the host knows it from then on. If you want to see the pricing before you test it, check [Pricing](/pricing). The current plan is pay per completed phone order, with no monthly fee or setup fee.

faq.q: Does ROAL take card numbers over the phone?
faq.a: No. ROAL does not take card numbers over the phone. Payment happens at pickup or however your restaurant already takes payment.

faq.q: Can it handle common Chinese takeout modifiers?
faq.a: Yes. It can take items, sizes, modifiers, and notes. That includes things like no onion, extra spicy, white rice, brown rice, and sauce changes when they are on your menu.

faq.q: What if a caller asks about something unusual?
faq.a: If ROAL cannot answer a question, it sends it to your inbox with context. You answer once, and the host can use that answer later.

faq.q: How do I turn it on for my current number?
faq.a: You claim the host, then forward your existing number to ROAL. You can forward all calls or only when busy or unanswered, and you can turn forwarding off any time.

faq.q: Is this only for big restaurant groups?
faq.a: No. ROAL is meant for independent restaurants too. It works for a single Chinese takeout shop, and it also works for more than one location.
